introSection.heading: Smart Casual & Formal Evenings at Sea
introSection.p1: One of the pleasures of a Princess Cruises holiday is the opportunity to enjoy relaxed days at sea and more elegant evenings onboard. You can spend the afternoon by the pool in resort wear, explore a destination in comfortable walking clothes and then change into a polished outfit for dinner.
introSection.p2: Princess Cruises keeps its evening dress code relatively straightforward, with two main designations: Smart Casual and Formal. Most evenings are Smart Casual, while selected nights are designated as Formal evenings, also known as Dress to Impress.
introSection.p3: Understanding the difference makes packing easier, particularly if you are planning a longer voyage, a special celebration or a cruise with several formal evenings. This guide explains what to wear, how many formal nights to expect, what is appropriate in the dining venues and what to pack for different destinations.
introSection.codeHeading: What Is the Dress Code on Princess Cruises?
introSection.codeP1: Princess Cruises uses two main evening dress codes: Smart Casual (polished everyday evening clothing suitable for a nice restaurant) and Formal (more elegant evening clothing for designated formal nights and selected onboard experiences).
introSection.codeP2: During the day, the atmosphere is generally relaxed. Resort wear, casual clothing, swimwear with appropriate cover-ups and comfortable shoes are suitable for many daytime settings.
introSection.codeP3: The dress code is most relevant when dining in the main dining rooms and specialty restaurants. Some individual venues and experiences may have additional requirements.

formalNightsShowcase.title: Princess Cruises Formal Nights: What Should You Wear?
formalNightsShowcase.subtitle: Formal evenings (Dress to Impress) are an opportunity to dress up for dinner, photographs and entertainment. Tuxedos and ballgowns are welcome, but dark suits and cocktail dresses are equally celebrated.

items.title: Formal Night Outfits for Women
items.description: Princess lists evening gowns, cocktail dresses, and elegant pantsuits as classic examples. Other sophisticated options, such as an elegant formal jumpsuit or refined evening separates, are also appropriate when meeting the dining venue's expectations.

items.title: Formal Night Outfits for Men
items.description: Recommended choices include tuxedos, dark suits, or dinner jackets paired with dress trousers. A well-fitted dark suit is a versatile and practical choice for guests who prefer not to pack a full tuxedo.

items.title: Formal Night Accessories
items.description: A few carefully chosen accessories complete your look without taking up valuable luggage space: dress shoes or elegant heels, a tie or bow tie, a dress belt, a small evening bag, jewellery or a watch, and a lightweight shawl or evening wrap that can be reused across multiple evenings.

formalScheduleTable.title: How Many Formal Nights Are on a Princess Cruise?
formalScheduleTable.note: These are general planning figures, not a guaranteed schedule for every departure. The exact evenings and onboard arrangements can vary by sailing. Check the Princess app and the daily onboard schedule for confirmed Dress to Impress evenings.

sevenNightEditorial.title: What Does This Mean for a Seven-Night Princess Cruise?
sevenNightEditorial.subtitle: A typical seven-night Princess sailing has two formal evenings and five smart casual nights. Here is a practical packing strategy to maximize style while minimizing luggage volume.

features.title: Two Formal Looks or One Versatile Outfit
features.description: Bring two formal outfits if you prefer a fresh look for each evening, or pack one versatile dark suit or little black dress paired with different shirts, ties, shawls, or jewelry to save luggage space.

features.title: Smart Casual Evening Rotations
features.description: Pack several Smart Casual tops and bottoms that coordinate effortlessly for the remaining five evenings. High-quality separates allow you to create distinct dinner looks without overpacking.

features.title: Daytime Resort & Port Attire
features.description: Bring lightweight, comfortable clothing for relaxing on sea days and exploring ashore. Repeating comfortable daytime staples keeps your suitcase manageable.

features.title: Smart Footwear Strategy
features.description: You do not need separate formal shoes for every night. A single pair of polished dress shoes, loafers, or elegant flats complements all your evening outfits across the voyage.

packingSituations.title: What Should You Pack for a Princess Cruise?
intro: A well-planned cruise wardrobe should cover three core situations: relaxed daytime activities onboard, Smart Casual and Formal evenings, and shore excursions with changing weather conditions.
The right combination depends on your itinerary, the length of your voyage and the destinations you plan to visit.

items.title: Daytime Clothing
paragraphs: For sea days and relaxed onboard activities, pack comfortable resort-style clothing made from breathable fabrics.

Recommended items include T-shirts and casual tops, shorts and lightweight trousers, sundresses and skirts, casual shirts, lightweight activewear, swimwear with cover-ups, and a light sweater for air-conditioned indoor spaces.

items.title: Evening Clothing
paragraphs: For a typical week-long Princess cruise, plan for two or three Smart Casual outfits, one or two Formal outfits, a versatile jacket, blazer or cardigan, comfortable evening shoes, and a small selection of accessories.
For longer cruises, you can bring additional outfits or plan to use the ship's convenient self-service and full-service laundry facilities.

items.title: Swimwear and Pool Clothing
paragraphs: If you expect to spend time around the pool, Sanctuary, or hot tubs, bring at least two swimsuits so one can dry while the other is in use, along with a lightweight cover-up, flip-flops or pool sandals, sunglasses, and a sun hat.
Remember that swimwear and beach attire are not appropriate for the main dining rooms during dinner.

items.title: Shore Excursion Clothing
paragraphs: Your port-day wardrobe should reflect the activities and climate on your itinerary. For city sightseeing, pack comfortable walking clothes and supportive shoes. For active excursions, consider suitable sportswear, hiking shoes, or weather-resistant clothing.

If visiting religious or cultural sites, check local dress expectations. Some destinations require covered shoulders, modest clothing, and longer skirts or trousers. A lightweight scarf or shawl is very useful.

items.title: Jackets and Weather Protection
paragraphs: Even warm-weather cruises can have cooler evenings, windy decks, and unexpected rain showers.

Consider packing a light sweater or cardigan, a wind-resistant jacket, a rain jacket or compact umbrella, and a warmer coat for cooler destinations. For Alaska and northern itineraries, pack versatile layers rather than relying on one heavy garment.

efficientPackingTips.title: Practical Tips for Packing More Efficiently
efficientPackingTips.subtitle: PACK SMARTER, TRAVEL LIGHTER, AND AVOID AIRLINE BAGGAGE FEES

steps.title: Choose Clothes That Mix and Match
steps.description: Select a consistent, cohesive colour palette so that tops, trousers, skirts, and blazers can be rotated into multiple fresh combinations throughout the cruise. Neutral tones work particularly well because they can be easily elevated with accessories.

steps.title: Pack Versatile Evening Outfits
steps.description: A single formal outfit can easily work for both formal evenings on a week-long cruise. Simply swap your tie, pocket square, shirt, or jewelry to create a refreshed aesthetic without wasting valuable suitcase space on extra bulky garments.

steps.title: Use Layers Instead of Bulky Garments
steps.description: For destinations with variable weather like Alaska or Northern Europe, layering thermal tops, fleece, and a waterproof shell provides greater temperature flexibility and packs much flatter than several heavy coats.

steps.title: Plan Around Onboard Laundry Facilities
steps.description: Princess ships feature convenient self-service launderettes (equipped with washers, dryers, irons, and detergent vending) alongside professional pressing and dry cleaning services, allowing you to pack half the luggage for longer itineraries.

steps.title: Keep Important Items in Your Carry-On
steps.description: Checked luggage is delivered to staterooms gradually throughout embarkation afternoon. Always keep your passport, cruise documentation, prescription medications, valuables, a change of clothes, and swimwear in your carry-on bag.

faqs.question: Does Princess Cruises have formal nights?
faqs.answer: Yes. Princess schedules selected Formal evenings, also called Dress to Impress nights. The number generally depends on the length of the cruise, with seven-night sailings typically featuring two formal evenings.

faqs.question: What is the dress code on a Princess cruise?
faqs.answer: Princess has two main evening dress codes: Smart Casual and Formal. Daytime attire is generally relaxed resort wear, while the evening dress code depends on the night and dining venue.

faqs.question: How many formal nights are on a seven-day Princess cruise?
faqs.answer: A typical seven-night cruise falls within Princess' seven-to-13-day category, which generally has two Formal evenings. Guests should check their specific sailing schedule on the Princess app for exact dates.

faqs.question: Do I need a tuxedo on Princess Cruises?
faqs.answer: No. A tuxedo is one suggested formal option for men, but a dark suit with a tie or a dinner jacket with dress slacks is equally appropriate and widely worn.

faqs.question: Can I wear jeans on Princess Cruises?
faqs.answer: Neat, non-distressed jeans may be appropriate for Smart Casual evenings in the main dining rooms. Jeans with holes, fraying, or tears are not welcomed in dining venues.

faqs.question: Can I wear shorts in the main dining room?
faqs.answer: Shorts are not welcomed in the main dining rooms during dinner under Princess' published dress guidance. Casual daytime venues like the buffet have more relaxed clothing expectations.

faqs.question: Can I skip formal night?
faqs.answer: Yes. Guests who prefer not to dress formally can choose casual dining options on formal evenings, including the World Fresh Marketplace buffet, International Café, poolside grills, or in-room dining.

faqs.question: Are formal nights compulsory?
faqs.answer: No. Formal nights are only enforced in the main dining rooms, specialty restaurants, and select premium culinary experiences (like 360 and Chef's Table Lumiere). Guests who prefer casual clothing can dine at informal venues.

faqs.question: What should I wear on a Princess Alaska cruise?
faqs.answer: Pack layers, waterproof outerwear, comfortable walking shoes, and warm accessories (gloves, beanie, fleece). You will also want Smart Casual and Formal outfits for evenings onboard.

faqs.question: Are swimsuits allowed in the dining room?
faqs.answer: No. Swimwear and beach attire are strictly prohibited in the main dining rooms and specialty restaurants during dinner. Cover-ups and footwear are required in all indoor public spaces.

faqs.question: Does Princess provide irons in the stateroom?
faqs.answer: No. For fire safety reasons, passenger staterooms do not contain clothes irons or steamers. However, Princess ships feature self-service launderettes equipped with ironing boards and irons, as well as full-service professional laundry pressing.
